Messages.Author: hardyrange
Messages.Body:
Hello out there,

my first quick "gut feeling" feedback re the proposed rule changes:

Proposed change #1: Timing during the influence phase
I do agree to this proposal, and the rationale behind it.

Proposed change #2: Anarch as a sect
First reaction is that this would create messy side effects - namely, the need to effectively change card text of the cards that now require an Independent vampire.
I am, right now, not sure if I see all the possible implications of this one, and if I see any VTES need to change anything with the rule (note that for me, aligning VTES with the role-playing game is not a reason...)

Proposed change #3: Caitiff as a clan
Agreed.

Proposed change #4: Recruit region
This would not change anything in real life, I guess. But it will make the rules somewaht clearer. So, agreed.

Best regards,

Hardy

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body:
#1: Agreed.

#2: Fine with the concept, but the execution looks a bit messy. Could anarchs be defined as a sub-sect of Independent so that we do not have to change all existing Independent cards?

EDIT: there is a grand total of 6 cards for independents, So I guess rewriting them would not be such a big effort. Besides, it opens some design space, as not all of those cards feel right for anarchs.

Banner of Neutrality: Independent only (and find a way to make it suck less.)
Community Justice: Independent only (see above.)
Exclusion Principle: Independent/Anarch.
Free States Rant: Anarch only (the only reason it is not is that it was printed before Anarchs were introduced.)
Reckless Agitation: Independent/Anarch.
Rise of the Nephtali: Independent only, because IIUC Nephtali is its own mini-sect.

#3: Agreed.

#4: No need for a special region, just as placing the ally in the Uncontrolled has always been a waste of time. Just state the rule that allies can't act the turn they are recruited, then let players track the game state in any way they see fit. Most of the time it is very easy to remember, and there is no reason to impose additional bookkeeping on everyone just for the occasional Mata Hari Recruits the World deck.

> #4: No need for a special region, just as placing the ally in the Uncontrolled has always been a waste of time. Just state the rule that allies can't act the turn they are recruited, then let players track the game state in any way they see fit. Most of the time it is very easy to remember, and there is no reason to impose additional bookkeeping on everyone just for the occasional Mata Hari Recruits the World deck.
>
Remembering that an ally can't act or putting it in the recruit region requires the same energy. Either way, you have to track that state.
The slight difference is that with your suggestion, the ally can block a minion controlled by another Methuselah acting the turn where the ally has been recruited (Enkil Cog, Madness Network). This is currently not the case.
Also, your suggestion affects allies that a War Ghoul can burn or not, or a Cry Wolf that could be turned into an Abomination.

But it's a suggestion worth considering.

Haqim's law: judgment requires independent assamite(s)

Reckless agitation seems like a major card for anarchs currently. Making it so that Anarchs couldn't call it would be a huge blow to anarch vote decks. Because the card is so strong, I'm tentatively ok with this. The change would be effectively nerfing Anarchs.

However, overall I am not a fan of this change, because there are so many cards that have 'independent anarch' in their card text. This change would confuse things once again.

> Ankha wrote:
> Remembering that an ally can't act or putting it in the recruit region requires the same energy.
> Either way, you have to track that state.
>
Not really, since some things are more intuitive than others. I'm pretty sure I've never, during the couple years that I've played VTES, put an ally to uncontrolled region. The current rule seems like unnecessary clutter to an already unnecessarily complex game.

You also have a delayed thing to remember (first putting ally to play to uncontrolled region, then moving it to controlled region). Instead of just putting it to play and considering whether it can or can't block when the situation arises. The latter allows shortcutting without endangering game state, the former requires you to do something largely superfluous EVERY TIME you play an ally. Adding obligatory things for player to do and remember that are largely irrelevant to how the game proceeds should be avoided.

> The slight difference is that with your suggestion, the ally can block a minion controlled by another Methuselah acting the turn where the ally has been recruited (Enkil Cog, Madness Network). This is currently not the case.
> But it's a suggestion worth considering.
>
This sounds like a corner case scenario. I would personally be fine in allowing allies to block in such a case. Its intuitive for allies to block since they are already in the game.

You obviously can play RotN without Anthelious, but generally you should not.

Logic behind it in decks I've seen was that you are counting of having Anthelios in play anyway (by having several copies as well as maybe liquidation - ashurs module to cycle to it) so it's easy to add RotN for some vote angle.

If you gameplan does not involve gehenna cards than adding several of them (one copy of Blood Trade will not be enough, obviously, to not be stuck with RotN in hand) for quite questionable gain is extremely not optimal.

Actually after some thought I'm not sure that removing independent clause will solve this problem anyway, so it'll be fine and easier to left it as it is. Anarchs got much more reliable Fee Stakes for the votes anyway.

NC Russia
